T132 (E2) done. Files: src/editor/pageBreakKeys.ts (new: extension PageBreakKeys, name pageBreakKeys, priority 1000, binds Shift-Enter to chain().focus().insertContent([pageBreak, paragraph]); declines inside tableCell/tableHeader so cells keep the ordinary soft break), src/editor/extensions.ts (registered immediately after StarterKit), src/editor/shortcuts.ts (hint "Insert page break": shift-enter glyph), tests/page-break.spec.ts.

FAIL-FIRST: on the pre-fix bundle (extension written but not registered) the spec failed at the intended assertion: manual-page-break count 0 and 0 page breaks after Shift+Enter, page count 1 (log ui3-e2/fail-first.log, playwright exit 1).

ACCEPTANCE, all run on the fixed tree: npx tsc --noEmit -p . exit 0 (ui3-e2/typecheck.log). npx vitest run src/editor: 7 files, 82 tests passed (ui3-e2/unit-editor.log). npx vite build exit 0 (ui3-e2/build-impl.log). PREVIEW(2) tests/page-break.spec.ts plus tests/footnotes.spec.ts: 5 passed, playwright exit 0 (ui3-e2/acceptance2.log). The spec covers: Shift+Enter makes one pageBreak between two paragraphs; page count reads 2 in page view; Cmd+Enter makes a hard break and no extra page break; the DOCX export of that project holds exactly one w:pageBreakBefore.

HARNESS FIX, no product change: the drafted spec asserted br count 1, but ProseMirror appends its own caret placeholder (br.ProseMirror-trailingBreak) at the end of a block that ends in a break, so the count was 1+1=2. The assertion now counts br:not(.ProseMirror-trailingBreak) and still proves the soft break exists. Do not loosen that again.

NOT DONE, deliberately: no change to src/Writer.tsx (not my path; the Page setup panel keeps its plain Insert page break button). No export change was needed: document.ts, docx.ts, pdf.ts and textExport.ts already handle pageBreak (confirmed by the DOCX assertion above). Native WebKit was not run; that belongs to T151 (V).

FOR OTHER LANES: the app schema now has a Shift-Enter keymap binding of priority 1000. Any test that typed a soft break with Shift-Enter relied on HardBreak before this; only Cmd-Enter is now a soft break. Inside a table cell Shift-Enter still makes a soft break.

DESIGN DOC (for D2/T150, design-system.md): Editor shortcuts -- Shift-Enter inserts a manual page break (a new page starts at the caret); the soft line break is Cmd-Enter. Inside a table cell Shift-Enter keeps the soft break, because a page break has no meaning inside a cell. The Settings > Shortcuts list shows Insert page break as read-only.
